title: Per-slot 'Start this check now' re-arms EVERY queued row for the application, not just the requested slot — AC1 "other slots untouched" violated
evidence:
rearm_queued_reference_calls.sql:8-13: "UPDATE reference_call
SET next_attempt_at = now(),
    updated_at = now()
WHERE application_id = $1
  AND status = 'queued'::reference_call_status
  AND taken_over_at IS NULL" (no slot filter); trigger.gleam:527-532: "// r1 (W6): ... the honest re-arm nudges every queued row to due-now so the sweep picks them up on the next tick" — run unconditionally after run_create_checks_slot, including the Some(slot) path; spec-rc4-3-row-actions.md:144: AC1 "starts that slot's check via the RC2.3 start API (`?slot=` — other slots untouched)".
detail: Creation is slot-scoped but the W6 re-arm is application-wide: the sibling slot's queued row is nudged due-now, so its referee gets an unsolicited early invite — contradicting AC1's "other slots untouched" and §7.4's per-reference "sends the invite now".
recommended_fix: Thread the requested slot into the re-arm (WHERE ref_slot = $2 when Some(slot)); keep the application-wide re-arm only for the no-slot whole-application start.

title: STILL PRESENT (r1): N18 — take-over confirm body still not §7.7 verbatim ('they' not 'he'); sibling §7.4 start confirm uses 'them' not 'her'
evidence: copy.gleam:828-829: "<> "'s details + the attempt log are yours. If they complete the form anyway, it still shows up here."" and copy.gleam:814: "<> "? We'll email and text them the form now."" vs ux-reference-checking-v1-2026-07-29.md:497 ("If he completes the form anyway, it still shows up here.") and :408 ("We'll email and text her the form now.").
detail: Name interpolation fixed (partial N18 fix), but 'he'→'they'/'her'→'them' persists. The cited rc4-2 W5 ruling covered objected copy ("asked us not to be contacted" — no pronoun), not the §7.4/§7.7 confirms; verbatim is the load-bearing invariant.
recommended_fix: Use 'he'/'her' per §7.4/§7.7 verbatim, or obtain an explicit ruling extending gender-neutrality to the confirm strings (and update the round's verbatim requirement).

title: STILL PRESENT (r1): N8 — spec item 6's additive shared-keys enumeration omits corrected_name
evidence: spec-rc4-3-row-actions.md:82-84: "6. **`shared/src/shared/reference_call.gleam`** — additive detail keys: `taken_over_at`, `contact_name`, `contact_email`, `contact_phone`, `corrected_email`, `corrected_phone`, `correction_cycles` (Option/Int, back-compat `optional_field` decoders). Encoder nullable." — while shared/src/shared/reference_call.gleam decodes/encodes corrected_name and supabase/migrations/20260812140000_reference_call_corrected_name.sql adds the column.
detail: corrected_name is still missing from item 6's enumeration although the same PR ships the column, the decoder key and the encoder key; a reader of the spec would not know the key exists.
recommended_fix: Add `corrected_name` to item 6's key list (and note correction_cycles is encoded as a non-nullable int).

title: PR's own spec artifacts still document the pre-W4 effective-contact rule, contradicting the implemented corrected-only rule
evidence: spec-rc4-3-row-actions.md:30: "the effective contact is `corrected ?? snapshot`" and epic-RC4-context.md:29: "Effective contact = corrected_* when present, else the immutable contact_* snapshot." vs sweep.gleam:705-729: "once a correction ran (correction_cycles >= 1) the snapshot is PROVEN DEAD ... a cleared channel stays absent (never falling back to the failed address)".
detail: The implemented W4 rule (corrected-only once correction_cycles >= 1, AD-7 never-re-contact) is not reflected in the spec's load-bearing rules; a future implementer reading them would re-contact a proven-dead channel after a cleared correction.
recommended_fix: Amend both spec artifacts: effective contact is corrected-only when correction_cycles >= 1, else corrected ?? snapshot.
